The max-row-norm argument bounds each changed entry by 50/100000 and the four-cell defect by -1/64+200/100000<0. Extracted standalone exact-rational checker tests each step including all 225 ordered minors. Proof quantifiers cover all point pairs via finitely many constant grid rectangles; no finite sampling is mistaken for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full HTML preprints arXiv:2306.09676v1 and arXiv:2205.01914v1 were directly inspected in their relevant definitions, examples and comparison theorems. The former proves only an MK-TP2/non-PMI failure via a Marshall–Olkin copula with a singular part, while the latter proves the strict hierarchy d-TP2=>MK-TP2. Neither states or implies a strictly positive absolutely continuous exchangeable d-TP2/non-PMI counterexample. Related searchable mathematical records and old own claims do not subsume this statement. Residual unknown-priority risk is acknowledged, not equated with independent originality certification.
residual_risks: An equivalent older TP2 matrix/coupling witness could exist under additive reflection-positivity or totally nonnegative matrix terminology.
The scope concerns piecewise-constant densities and does not claim all smooth or Archimedean density-TP2 models violate PMI.

value.rationale: PMI controls reflection-based concordance inequalities while d-TP2 is the strongest standard density-level positive dependence property. The strictly positive exchangeable witness demonstrates that multiplicative total positivity and the PMI additive reflection inequality differ even under strong natural regularity/symmetry constraints; this is a structural boundary for use of PMI in dependence modeling. It is sharper than the existing singular MK-TP2 example without asserting a paper-sized contribution, minimal grid or smoothness.
